summary: Today’s PaymentsDive recap: 8 new stories, with focus on regulation, product + fintech innovation.

articles.title: Butter Payments has been sold
articles.description: The company was purchased last month, said its former chief executive, Charles Rosenblatt, who noted intensifying competitive pressures.

articles.title: PayPal isn’t agile enough, CEO says
articles.description: As part of his turnaround efforts, Enrique Lores said Monday the digital payments company requires faster decisions and clearer accountability.

articles.title: Ramp seeks bank charter
articles.description: Ramp applied with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency for a national trust bank charter on Friday.

articles.title: Utah forms digital ID consortium
articles.description: The state is using its digital identity law as a model for having individuals, not governments, control their personal data, Utah’s chief privacy officer said.

articles.title: The 67% signal: Why card issuers should act on flexible credentials
articles.description: 67% want one card for debit, credit and BNPL. Don’t let a competitor give it to them first.

articles.title: AI’s real opportunity in payments is giving experts back their time
articles.description: Advancing operational efficiency through intelligent guidance on errors and exception handling.

articles.title: Visa, Mastercard urge court to approve fee settlement
articles.description: The card networks contend Walmart and trade groups want to scuttle a legal pact over card swipe fees using recycled arguments the court has rejected.

articles.title: Congress should examine EWA bill
articles.description: “Combining employer-integrated solutions and direct-to-consumer products under a single, relaxed standard weakens consumer safety,” writes an industry executive.
